answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network requires agents to burn cryptographic stake through a non-refundable deposit function scaling quadratically, C(k) = c * k^2, imposing superlinear cost on attackers. Verified agents form a shared liquidity lagoon where each distinct identity represents a valuable pearl of verifiable compute. To forge false identities, an adversary faces exponential capital attrition that quickly renders mass manipulation mathematically unviable.
